intended_object: The canonical group isomorphism between the kernel of the determinant restricted to O(Q), seen as a subgroup of O(Q), and SO(Q) = O(Q) ∩ ker(det), seen as a subgroup of Aut_R(M). Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: This definition is bookkeeping between two encodings in the library, not a mathematical object in its own right. `specialOrthogonalWithin Q` is defined as `(orthogonalDet Q).ker`, a subgroup of the subtype `orthogonalGroup Q`. `specialOrthogonalGroup Q` is defined as `orthogonalGroup Q ⊓ LinearEquiv.det.ker`, a subgroup of `M ≃ₗ[R] M`. On paper these are the same group, {g ∈ O(Q) : det g = 1}, and the map between them is the identity. The Lean term only moves between the two encodings. It rewrites with `specialOrthogonalWithin_eq_subgroupOf` (via `MulEquiv.subgroupCongr`) and then uses Mathlib's `Subgroup.subgroupOfEquivOfLe`, which identifies `H.subgroupOf K` with `H` when `H ≤ K`. Each element is sent to itself, so the construction is correct and the docstring is accurate. Its only role is to transport results between the library's two presentations of SO(Q). Mathlib has the general tool (`Subgroup.subgroupOfEquivOfLe`) but no dedicated counterpart for this particular identification.
